independent.subject: one changeable vote per member; set semantics A->B
independent.detail: Alice voted a (a=1,b=0), changed to b (a=0,b=1) with no total growth. Bob voted a online then changed to b while actually browser-offline. Final canonical state: a=0, b=2, total 2 votes; stored rows show exactly two vote rows (one per principal) and maintained pollTallies b=2 with no 'a' row. API-level repetition of the same state also left a=0,b=1 unchanged on a separate control poll.

independent.subject: repeat of same chosen option adds no second vote/count
independent.detail: After settlement Bob re-clicked the same option b in the UI: tallies stayed a=0,b=2,total 2 and no pending operation remained. Independent API repeat of polls.vote with the identical option produced no tally change (unique (pollId,userId) upsert).

independent.subject: offline vote durability: pending survives close/reopen offline and settles once on reconnect
independent.detail: Playwright context set actually offline (app status text 'offline'); Bob's vote became a pending operation 251794fe-c566-484d-8ebd-05284d6dcea5 shown as busy/selected without a synthetic tally bump. The page was closed and a new page opened while still offline: the app shell was restored from the service-worker cache, the session persisted, and the same durable operation ID was still queued. On reconnect the queue drained once (pending empty) and the tally moved to b=2 exactly once; no duplicate vote rows exist. No synthetic network fault was substituted.

defects.title: Migration driver persona list contains two non-existent accounts
defects.reproduction: m7/migrate.mjs iterates ['alice','bob','carol','dave','eve','frank','grace','heidi']; the seeded accounts are dave/erin/frank/grace/henry. The retained m7/migration.json ends with error 'E_AUTH_INVALID: invalid email or password'.
defects.practicalImplication: The builder's persona-sweep coverage argument is weaker than stated because the sweep aborted after the first two personas; coverage is nevertheless complete here only because a physical census shows exactly two conversations existed. On a database where a conversation was visible only to a later persona, this driver would have silently missed it.
evidence: grading/results/replay-migration.json (my sweep with the correct persona names)

defects.title: Backfill cannot migrate a conversation with 201 or more visible messages
defects.reproduction: snapback/conversations.q backfillCount counts `first 201 by byVisible` and rejects with BACKFILL_CHUNK_TOO_LARGE at >= 201; no chunked or resumable path exists.
defects.practicalImplication: The day-two migration works for this prepared starter database only. Any realistic conversation over 200 visible messages cannot be migrated with the shipped mutation, and messages.send/polls.create reject unbackfilled conversations (COUNT_NOT_MIGRATED), so such a conversation would become unwritable after the schema change. Neither the builder nor I exercised a reduced-chunk attempt because no conversation exceeded the guard.

defects.title: An old client's queued operation parks indefinitely with no terminal outcome after a schema/program identity change
defects.reproduction: Reopen the saved pre-M7 profile offline at http://127.0.0.1:54910 (operation 731cbc48-b0ea-4e0a-819d-a74e5bc59a19 present), then serve a migrated database at that origin and reconnect. Over ~60 s online plus a reload the operation stays in state.pending, never commits (server DM still has 6 messages and no m7-old-client-... message) and is never rejected.
defects.practicalImplication: A user who composed a message before a deployment sees it queued forever with no error and no delivery; the app offers no surface to retire or resubmit it, and the platform provides no terminal receipt. Parked is not automatic compatibility. The builder's API.md documents parking honestly and did not claim old-client success.

defects.title: Resource completeness flag is false on fresh single-row/paged results
defects.reproduction: messages.latest via the separately installed client returns status 'ready', fresh true, data present, complete false (grading/results/custom-api-results-grader.json); API.md documents the same behaviour for large paginated refreshes and src/acquire.ts contains an explicit workaround.
defects.practicalImplication: Applications cannot rely on the SDK completeness flag to decide acquisition is finished, so every client must verify IDs itself; this is an ergonomic cost carried by the app, not a defect introduced by M7.

defects.title: Nonmember poll read is denied by never completing rather than by an explicit error
defects.reproduction: dave (nonmember) calls polls.get: the resource returns ok with complete=false and no data instead of an explicit NOT_MEMBER error, unlike polls.vote/create which return explicit codes.
defects.practicalImplication: Authorization holds (no data leaks), but a client cannot distinguish denial from a slow/incomplete resource without extra logic.

defects.title: Chat settings count is only visible while the settings panel is toggled open and resets when the conversation is reselected
defects.reproduction: Open a conversation, press Chat settings (count appears), switch conversation and back: the panel is closed again and the count is not shown until re-toggled.
defects.practicalImplication: Minor discoverability issue only; the value itself was reachable and correct at every checkpoint. It also caused one of my waits to time out before I re-read the value successfully (retained in grading/results/poll-browser-grader.json).

overallIndependentAssessment.selectedTextWebSubset: All nine selected m7 assertions in the frozen text/web subset were independently reproduced as passing on the frozen final app, including a real migration replay on an isolated copy of the supplied pre-M7 database, complete preservation of all 16 preexisting message rows and every required exported field/control for all three personas, canonical counts 6/9 -> 10 -> 11 with reachable UI and API agreement, genuine browser-offline vote durability with a single settlement, and the 25 previously passing selected regressions.
overallIndependentAssessment.qualifications: Findings are limited to this small prepared starter database and the text/web projection. The migration approach does not generalize past 200 visible messages (D2), the old-client pending operation parks without resolution (D3), and the builder's migration sweep contained a persona-name error (D1).
